metrics.guard: Track alongside the acceptance-proposal domain's own check-strength diagnostics (owner_feedback/public_contracts); a jump in this rate coincident with new/replaced acceptance files for the same milestones is flagged for manual review before being credited to any repair-side lever.
metrics.verifier_note: Correct in substance and correctly guardrail (easy to game via weaker acceptance files); source needs to be explicit that the acceptance-ran flag is only in the per-check evidence file, not the ledger row.

metrics.definition: Restrict the denominator to the SAME population as build.apply_rate (status=acceptance_passed AND autonomy=propose AND apply grant true AND draft files within scope AND recheck_only=false), not all build.checked with status=acceptance_passed. As written, the denominator also includes acceptance_passed drafts where the OUTER gate (grant/autonomy/apply-flag/scope, lines 737-739) was never satisfied at all — cases that never even reach the 'valid' computation this metric targets, silently diluting the block rate with unrelated owner-configuration non-applies (see added metric build.grant_mismatch_apply_skip_rate for that separate case).

metrics.name: Auto-apply conversion rate
metrics.definition: Note an edge case: a build.advanced event can fire via _unchanged_verdict's cache-hit path (building.py:328-330) when an owner re-triggers a build on an already acceptance_passed, still-waiting draft after changing autonomy/apply settings — with NO new build.checked event accompanying that particular apply. Over a bounded reporting window this decouples the numerator (build.advanced count) from the denominator (build.checked count) unless each build.advanced is joined back to the ORIGINAL build.checked event it re-applies (which may fall outside the window), not just counted against same-window build.checked rows.
metrics.source: building.py:735-774 (_apply_if_current, not 726-762); building.py:314-335, specifically :328-330 (_unchanged_verdict can ALSO trigger _apply_if_current / build.advanced, reusing a PRIOR check's cached acceptance_passed verdict, with no fresh build.checked in the same call).
metrics.min_sample: ~20-30 acceptance_passed checks under an apply-enabled grant
metrics.gaming_risk: Easiest metric in this domain to game by weakening the acceptance file itself (any candidate passes, so anything applies).
metrics.guard: NEVER read without build.acceptance_pass_rate on the same slice; a trial is only credited for this metric moving if acceptance pass criteria are provably unchanged (same acceptance_sha256/acceptance_bundle across the comparison window).
metrics.verifier_note: Core definition and the primary/gameability framing are sound; the cache-hit reapplication path is a real, non-obvious source of numerator/denominator mismatch in windowed reporting.

metrics.name: Stale-verdict rate
metrics.definition: count(build.checked where status=stale) + count(build.current_files_checked where status=stale), divided by count(build.checked)+count(build.current_files_checked). This IS already recorded via the existing ledger status field for both event types — no new instrumentation needed for the aggregate rate. What still needs instrumentation is distinguishing WHICH of the four stale causes fired (see added metric build.stale_cause_distribution), since only the bare function return value (never persisted) carries that detail.
metrics.source: building.py:195,198,204,211-212 (FOUR distinct 'stale' returns, not three); building.py:717-719 and :597-599 (build.checked and build.current_files_checked DO record status='stale' — every non-exception verify_draft return, including all four stale branches and all three 'unsupported' branches, flows through _save_checked_draft's unconditional ledger.append at line 717-719, or through review_current_files' own ledger.append at 597-599); building.py:314-335 (_unchanged_verdict never calls verify_draft — it reuses the cached 'verification' dict directly, so it must be EXCLUDED from, not included in, the denominator).
metrics.min_sample: ~15-20 stale events before treating a rate change as real
metrics.gaming_risk: A fast-but-racy author path could be judged fast overall while quietly pushing its cost into repeated stale rechecks that the owner has to notice and retry manually.
metrics.guard: Any drop in build.time_to_green must be checked against this metric staying flat or falling too; needs a new ledger field/event distinguishing outcome_cause on every stale return before it can be computed precisely.
metrics.verifier_note: The catalogue undersells this metric's availability (called it needs_instrumentation) while also getting the denominator backwards: it claims _unchanged_verdict's cache path should be INCLUDED as a verify_draft call, but that function is specifically the F14 fix that skips calling verify_draft on an unchanged waiting draft (confirmed against JOURNEY_LOG.md:135, '20:20Z F14 committed: a scheduled round no longer rechecks an unchanged waiting draft').

metrics.verifier_note: Same root problem as build.allowance_exhaustion_rate (an eligibility condition computed by a stateless query function, never logged) was caught there but missed here; the denominator is currently uncountable, not merely 'derivable'.

metrics.gaming_risk: Same as build.calls_to_green but broader: a change could move calls out of the 'build' role into 'plan' or 'acceptance' roles and look like an improvement on the narrower build-only metric while this total stays flat or rises.
metrics.guard: Always read next to build.calls_to_green_by_model; a gap opening between the two localizes exactly which role absorbed the shifted cost.

metrics.name: Total cost, milestone creation to applied
metrics.definition: Sum of est_usd over every instrument.call whose 'key' field starts with 'draft-<m>-' for milestone m (runesmith/app/planner.py:521 defines request_key = f'draft-{milestone_id}-{time.time_ns()}'), for all roles (plan, repair, kaizen if attributable, acceptance), from milestone.added to the applied draft. Calls with cost_status other than 'reported_attempt_reconciled'/'reported_aggregate_only' (see runesmith/inference_usage.py:33-62) are excluded from the sum and counted separately as e2e.milestone_cost_coverage_gap.
metrics.source: instrument.call {key, est_usd, accounting} (runesmith/app/workspace.py:564-566); cost qualification runesmith/inference_usage.py:23-68.
metrics.min_sample: 20+ applied milestones per slice; noise from provider pricing variance and partial cost reporting (aggregate_mismatch/cached_unverified rows).
metrics.gaming_risk: A generation could learn to make cheap, low-effort attempts that fail checks quietly and get silently retried (moving cost into an uncounted or misattributed bucket) rather than genuinely cutting cost.
metrics.guard: Watch alongside build.calls_to_green and inference.aggregate_mismatch_rate; a falling milestone_cost_usd with a rising aggregate_mismatch_rate or check_fail_rate is a red flag, not an improvement.

metrics.name: Total lead time, milestone creation to applied
metrics.definition: For each milestone id m, utc(draft.applied whose draft.milestone==m and follows a milestone.updated{id:m,status:'done'}) minus utc(milestone.added{id:m}). Excludes milestones never applied (right-censored, reported separately as e2e.full_pipeline_success_rate's complement). Report the distribution, not just the mean.
metrics.source: milestone.added (runesmith/app/workspace.py:737), draft.applied (runesmith/app/workspace.py:1203), milestone.updated status:done (runesmith/app/workspace.py:722, via update_milestone); join key = draft['milestone'] read from drafts/<id>/DRAFT.json (runesmith/app/workspace.py:1148) since the ledger draft.created/draft.applied events themselves do not carry the milestone field.
metrics.min_sample: at least 20 applied milestones per slice before comparing two conditions (matches the trial machinery's own min_per_arm=10 doubled for a two-sided-in-spirit business comparison); noise sources: milestone size/difficulty variance, provider load (inference.milliner_queue_dwell_s), and how many corrections/escalations/revisions a milestone happens to trigger.
metrics.gaming_risk: Could be gamed by silently shrinking milestones into trivially small ones (more, faster, smaller applied changes) without shrinking real project scope, inflating apparent speed while owner value per milestone falls.
metrics.guard: Pair with mapping_planning.planner.milestone_lines_changed and build.milestone_lead_time_distribution so a drop in e2e lead time that comes with a matching drop in change size is flagged, not celebrated.

metrics.name: Share of milestone lead time spent waiting on the owner
metrics.definition: Share of e2e.milestone_lead_time_total during which the milestone's draft/proposal was in a state requiring owner action: manual.set_aside/manual.skipped active, an acceptance.proposed awaiting acceptance.approved/discarded, or a note.added targeting this milestone unresolved (note.resolved not yet seen).
metrics.source: manual.set_aside, manual.skipped, acceptance.proposed/approved/discarded, note.added/note.resolved (ledger kinds; call sites in runesmith/app/workspace.py and runesmith/app/acceptance_proposals.py).
metrics.min_sample: 20+ milestones; noise from owner's own availability (evenings/weekends), not the system.
metrics.gaming_risk: A system could be tuned to auto-approve or skip acceptance review to shrink this number while quietly lowering checks.approval_rate quality; must not be optimized alone.
metrics.guard: Pair with checks.approval_rate and owner_reliability.rescue_rate; owner_wait_share should fall only if approval quality (not just approval speed) holds.

metrics.name: Time from milestone creation to first authoring attempt
metrics.definition: utc(first draft.created with milestone==m) minus utc(milestone.added{id:m}). Captures the planning/acceptance-authoring overhead that build.time_to_green (which starts at 'first attempt') does not.
metrics.source: milestone.added (runesmith/app/workspace.py:737), draft.created + DRAFT.json milestone field (runesmith/app/workspace.py:1146-1153).
metrics.gaming_risk: Low; mainly reveals queueing/scheduling delay.
metrics.guard: n/a (diagnostic)

metrics.name: Share of applied milestones later reopened
metrics.definition: count(milestone ids with a milestone.updated{status:'done'} followed later by another milestone.updated{status: not 'done'} for the same id, or a later draft.created whose milestone==m after m was already applied) / count(milestones ever applied).
metrics.source: milestone.updated (runesmith/app/workspace.py:722), draft.created (runesmith/app/workspace.py:1152).
metrics.gaming_risk: A generation could be tuned to never mark anything 'done' again once applied (refusing legitimate rework) purely to keep this low.
metrics.guard: Watch against mapping_planning.planner.milestone_completion_rate; a falling rework rate with a falling completion rate is not an improvement.

metrics.name: Milestone wall time split by pipeline stage
metrics.definition: For each applied milestone, the share of its total e2e.milestone_lead_time_total spent in each pipeline_stage bucket (planning, acceptance_authoring, building, checking, escalation_or_correction, owner_review). Mirrors self_improvement.value_stream_model_share/signal_share/other_share but for the main product loop rather than the Kaizen loop.
metrics.unit: ratio (per stage, sums to 1 per milestone)
metrics.source: same event set as e2e.milestone_lead_time_total, bucketed by which event pair bounds each stage.
metrics.instrumentation_needed: a per-event 'stage' tag (or a documented mapping from event kind to stage) so a dashboard need not hand-encode the event sequence; today it is derivable only by writing that mapping once in analysis code, not recorded at write time.
metrics.gaming_risk: None directly (diagnostic), but a shrinking 'building' share paired with a growing 'escalation_or_correction' share would mask a regression if only the primaries were watched.
metrics.guard: n/a (diagnostic)

metrics.name: Applied milestones per wall-clock hour of active session
metrics.definition: count(draft.applied) / total hours across studio.opened...studio.round session spans in the same window, restricted to sessions with at least one applied draft. This is the 'production iteration speed' number the owner asked for directly ('speed, efficiency, production iteration specs').
metrics.source: studio.opened, studio.round (session bounds; ledger kinds, call sites in runesmith/app/server.py or workspace.py), draft.applied (runesmith/app/workspace.py:1203).
metrics.min_sample: 10+ sessions per slice; noise from session length variance and owner-review pauses (see e2e.owner_wait_share as a covariate to control for).
metrics.gaming_risk: Splitting one real milestone into many trivially small 'applied' drafts inflates this without adding value.
metrics.guard: Read together with mapping_planning.planner.milestone_lines_changed (median change size); a rising throughput with falling median size is a Goodhart signal, not a win.

metrics.name: Audited-cost coverage rate
metrics.definition: count(terminal instrument.call events where the 'accounting' field is present/non-null) / count(terminal instrument.call events), per instrument and per instrument kind. An event has 'accounting' only when MillinerInstrument._response() set it (instruments.py:236-241); OpenAICompatInstrument (359-361) and OllamaInstrument (427-428) never populate it.
metrics.source: runesmith/instruments.py:236-241 vs 359-361 and 427-428; runesmith/app/workspace.py:564-566 ('accounting' passes the whitelist when present).
metrics.min_sample: at least 30 terminal calls per instrument before reporting a percentage; report 'insufficient data' below that.
metrics.gaming_risk: none directly gameable by a model call -- the risk is upstream: an owner or router-policy trial quietly preferring non-Milliner paid routes lowers coverage while increasing real, invisible spend.
metrics.guard: must be read together with inference.unaudited_paid_spend_share -- falling coverage alongside rising direct-paid-route volume is a red flag, not noise; falling coverage from more LOCAL/free traffic is fine.

metrics.name: Cost-accounting mismatch rate
metrics.definition: Add the same explicit scope as token_accounting_completeness_rate: meaningful only over Milliner-routed events, since 'accounting.cost_status' does not exist for OpenAICompat/Ollama calls.
metrics.source: runesmith/inference_usage.py:56-58 (complete and any(aggregate[f]!=result[f]) => 'aggregate_mismatch')
metrics.gaming_risk: none directly gameable; a rising rate flags a provider/gateway data-quality regression that would silently corrupt every cost metric downstream if ignored
metrics.guard: any cost_per_successful_call improvement must be re-verified as not simply riding a rising mismatch rate toward under-reporting
metrics.verifier_note: Formula fine; needs the scope stated so it isn't read as an all-traffic number.

metrics.name: Recorded route-availability status mix
metrics.source: runesmith/app/inference_availability.py:42-143, esp. 115-130 (status derivation), 50 (default 'unknown') and 16 (MAX_RECEIPTS=100)
metrics.min_sample: n/a, it is itself a distribution; read the 'coverage' object (scanned/matching/omitted/unreadable) alongside it before trusting the shares
metrics.gaming_risk: this is explicitly a read-only, non-probing projection (module docstring, inference_availability.py:1-5) — 'a past success or elapsed wait does not promise quota' (line 142), so it must never be used to auto-select a route without a fresh check
metrics.guard: never fed into an automated routing decision directly; it is a display/diagnostic surface, per the module's own caution string
metrics.verifier_note: Accurate as stated.

metrics.name: Ticket binding-mismatch rate
metrics.source: runesmith/milliner_jobs.py:79-83,123-128 (binding_mismatch when the authenticated agent identity returned doesn't match); runesmith/app/inference_accounting.py:16-19 (STATES includes 'binding_mismatch')
metrics.min_sample: n/a — this should be at or near zero at all times; any nonzero sustained rate is itself the finding
metrics.gaming_risk: not gameable in a useful direction; this is a security/identity property of the ticket protocol, not a tunable performance number
metrics.guard: any self-improvement trial that touches routing must confirm this stays at its current (near-zero) level — it is a hard guardrail, not a target to move
metrics.verifier_note: Accurate; correctly scoped to receipt-file state, not a ledger event.

metrics.name: Cached-response rate
metrics.definition: Scope explicitly to Milliner-routed calls, where 'cached' is a meaningful signal: count(Milliner-routed instrument.call where cached=true) / count(Milliner-routed instrument.call). Pooling in OpenAICompat/Ollama calls (which never report caching) inflates the denominator with calls neither confirmed cached nor confirmed fresh, silently understating the rate rather than reporting 'not applicable' for that kind.
metrics.source: 'cached' confirmed in the ledger whitelist (workspace.py:565) and confirmed set by MillinerInstrument (instruments.py:240) -- but OpenAICompatInstrument (359-361) and OllamaInstrument (427-428) never set 'cached' at all; for those calls the key is simply absent (not stored as false).
metrics.gaming_risk: a rising cached rate can make cost_per_successful_call look artificially good only if cached calls are wrongly included in the cost average — inference_usage.py already excludes their tokens/cost, so the guard is to confirm that exclusion holds, not to double-count savings
metrics.guard: cross-checked against inference_usage.py's own null-out behaviour for cached receipts before ever crediting a cost saving to a routing change
metrics.verifier_note: Guard about inference_usage.py's null-out behaviour is correctly confirmed, but the formula's population wrongly mixes in a whole instrument class that never contributes a genuine signal.

metrics.name: Model calls attempted
metrics.definition: count(instrument.call) grouped by role/instrument/provider -- NOT by 'kind': 'kind' is never written to the ledger event (workspace.py:564-566's whitelist has exactly 18 fields and 'kind' is not one of them, even though Instrument.identity() at instruments.py:157-158 includes it in the pre-filter event). To slice by kind (openai/ollama/milliner/manual/scripted), join the recorded 'instrument' name to config['instruments'][name]['kind'] as configured TODAY, which misattributes any historical call made under a since-changed instrument definition.
metrics.source: runesmith/app/workspace.py:544-566 (record_call, ledger.append('instrument.call', ...)); runesmith/instruments.py:529-532 (Router._attempt calls self._on_call once per rotation)
metrics.min_sample: raw count, no statistical minimum; trend over >=50 calls before reading a rate change as real
metrics.gaming_risk: volume alone rewards making more, possibly redundant, calls; never used alone to judge an improvement
metrics.guard: always paired with success/cost/latency per call, never optimised by itself
metrics.verifier_note: Core citation and 'one event per rotation' claim both check out exactly. The one inaccuracy is the implied ability to group directly by 'kind', which is silently dropped before the ledger write.

metrics.name: Role censor rate (gave up entirely)
metrics.definition: Same target. Note a crude proxy is derivable today by grouping instrument.call events on their shared 'key' field (constant across retries, instruments.py:530) and checking whether every attempt for that key has error_kind='transport' with attempt reaching len(DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S)+1=8 -- but this can't distinguish genuine exhaustion from an early no_retry short-circuit, since that flag is also dropped from the ledger (same gap as pre_admission_refusal_rate). The dedicated event already recommended is still the correct fix.
metrics.source: runesmith/instruments.py:54-59,505-509 (TransportCensored raised after the full backoff ladder); runesmith/app/building.py:407-414 (only place I found it caught and logged, as a string)
metrics.min_sample: n/a until instrumented; once recorded, 20+ role invocations per cell
metrics.gaming_risk: a route that fails fast with 'config' instead of exhausting retries would lower this number without actually improving anything for the owner
metrics.guard: exact instrumentation needed: have Router.call (instruments.py:491-509) append a structured ledger event (e.g. 'instrument.censored') with role, the instruments tried, and total attempts, instead of only raising an exception for the caller to catch and stringify
metrics.verifier_note: Original assessment was accurate and appropriately skeptical; confirms rather than replaces the need for real instrumentation.

metrics.name: Configuration-refusal rate
metrics.source: runesmith/instruments.py:269-285 (_permanent()), 328-332 (OpenAICompatInstrument preflight), 396-401 (OllamaInstrument preflight), 348-352 (config classification on response)
metrics.min_sample: 30+ calls per project_size_band; this error is close to deterministic given prompt size vs a fixed window, so smaller samples are still informative once size is held constant
metrics.gaming_risk: could be gamed by silently truncating prompts rather than refusing — that would move failures into output_failure_rate/build.checked instead, so both must be watched together
metrics.guard: paired with inference.output_failure_rate — a drop here that is matched by a rise there means requests are being shrunk, not fixed
metrics.verifier_note: Accurate. Unlike request_oversize_block_rate, this only needs the already-recorded error_kind category, not message text.

metrics.name: Cost per attempted call
metrics.source: runesmith/inference_usage.py:1-6 (module docstring: 'never infer a bill or apply today's prices'), 59-60 (cost_status values); runesmith/app/inference_accounting.py:126-133 (summary.estimated_usd, a subtotal only, explicitly captioned 'not a bill')
metrics.gaming_risk: routing to instruments with incomplete cost reporting (e.g. manual/local, which never carry est_usd) would make this look artificially low while doing nothing to reduce real spend on the paid routes still in use
metrics.guard: always reported alongside inference.token_accounting_completeness_rate so a low cost figure with low completeness is flagged, not trusted
metrics.verifier_note: Formula and completeness caveat right, but gaming_risk understates the gap: real paid spend through any directly-configured OpenAI-compatible instrument is invisible, not just local/manual routes. See added inference.unaudited_paid_spend_share.

metrics.name: Cost per successful call
metrics.source: same as inference.cost_per_call, combined with the 'ok' field
metrics.gaming_risk: same as cost_per_call, plus: a cheaper-but-worse model that needs 3 retries to get one success can still show a low 'per call' cost while its true cost (counting the failed attempts) is high — must be computed per *role invocation*, counting all attempts' cost against the eventual success, not per raw call
metrics.guard: paired with inference.role_fallback_depth so the true, attempt-inclusive cost of a success is visible, and with the cross-domain build.checked pass rate so a cheap wrong answer isn't counted as a win
metrics.verifier_note: Same correction as cost_per_call, more sharply since this is primary: a router-policy trial could show falling 'cost' purely by shifting calls to a direct paid route with zero cost visibility -- must be paired with the new inference.unaudited_paid_spend_share, not just role_fallback_depth.

metrics.name: Duplicate/aliased receipt rate
metrics.source: runesmith/app/inference_accounting.py:90-111 (union-find over request/ticket identity), 57 (coverage dict)
metrics.gaming_risk: none; purely a data-hygiene diagnostic for whether the receipt-collapsing logic is working as intended
metrics.guard: a rising 'conflicting' state count (inference_accounting.py:114-119, distinct from ordinary duplicates) should halt trust in cost/success numbers for that instrument until resolved
metrics.verifier_note: Accurate. The 'conflicting' state this entry's own guard references has no formal id anywhere in the catalogue -- added inference.receipt_conflict_rate to close that gap.

metrics.name: Structured error-detail capture rate
metrics.definition: Once a structured 'error_reason' field (truncated/invalid_json/schema_failed/bad_request/oversize_preflight/context_overflow/model_not_found/other) is added per the corrections to inference.truncation_rate/schema_invalid_json_rate/request_oversize_block_rate/ollama_context_truncation_proxy_rate: count(instrument.call where error_kind in ('output','config') and error_reason != 'other') / count(instrument.call where error_kind in ('output','config')). Guards against the classifier silently falling into an unclassified bucket as new providers/wordings appear.
metrics.source: runesmith/instruments.py:44-51 (classify()'s marker-list approach, which a provider wording change can silently miss). The proposed 'error_reason' field does not exist yet; this metric is only meaningful after that instrumentation lands.
metrics.min_sample: at least 30 output/config errors per instrument before reporting a percentage.
metrics.gaming_risk: none directly; the risk is the reverse -- silently classifying everything as 'other' would hide the very failure modes several other metrics in this catalogue depend on.
metrics.guard: n/a -- this is itself the guard for those other metrics' new instrumentation.

metrics.name: Free-tier quota headroom used
metrics.source: runesmith/instruments.py:327-332 (the ratio computed inline but not persisted); runesmith/app/providers.py:39-40 (the one hard-coded provider ceiling in the codebase)
metrics.min_sample: n/a until instrumented; 20+ calls per size band once added
metrics.gaming_risk: none once recorded, beyond the general risk of shrinking requests to look good on paper while losing context the model needed
metrics.guard: only meaningful for providers with a codified ceiling; do not extrapolate to OpenRouter/Gemini/Mistral, whose limits are not tracked in code (see notes)
metrics.verifier_note: Accurate as stated.

metrics.name: Milliner internal model-fallback usage
metrics.definition: Add explicit scope: computable ONLY for Milliner-routed instrument.call events. OpenAICompatInstrument (receipt at 360-361) and OllamaInstrument (receipt at 427-428) never set an 'accounting' field at all, so they are structurally absent from both numerator and denominator, not counted as depth=1.
metrics.source: runesmith/instruments.py:179-185,196-199 (fallback_models chain built into the request), 236-241 (receipt['provider_attempts']=meta.get('attempts',[])); runesmith/inference_usage.py:25-27,32,40-43 ('attempts' qualification)
metrics.gaming_risk: padding the fallback_models list with easy models makes 'eventually answered' rates look good while hiding that the primary model is unreliable
metrics.guard: always reported alongside which position in the chain actually answered (primary vs which fallback), not just a fell-through/did-not flag
metrics.verifier_note: Citations accurate; definition should state its Milliner-only scope explicitly.

metrics.name: Kaizen-role cost/latency/success trend across repair-organ generations
metrics.source: runesmith/app/workspace.py:564-566 (instrument.call with role='kaizen'); generation.activated/trial.opened/trial.closed_by_owner/trial.rejected (ledger event names given in the task's own list)
metrics.min_sample: needs several generations' worth of kaizen calls (per generation.activated crossings) before a trend is more than one data point per generation; treat single-generation deltas as anecdotal
metrics.gaming_risk: a generation that simply reduces kaizen-role call volume (fewer, smaller improvement attempts) would show 'improved' cost/latency while doing less actual self-improvement work — must be read alongside inference.call_volume for the same role
metrics.guard: paired with inference.call_volume(role='kaizen') and, cross-domain, with the trial's own Fisher-test result (runesmith/kaizen/trial.py, not read here) so a favorable inference trend is never substituted for the trial's actual pass/fail verdict
metrics.verifier_note: Appropriately hedged already; the one checkable citation confirms cleanly.

metrics.name: Connection-test pass rate
metrics.source: runesmith/app/workspace.py:510-517 (test_instrument, ledger.append('instrument.tested', {'name','ok'})); runesmith/app/providers.py:147-162 (test_instrument: one tiny JSON call through the real instrument)
metrics.min_sample: 5+ tests per instrument (these are owner-triggered, so naturally low-frequency)
metrics.gaming_risk: a trivial fixed prompt ('Reply with {"ok": true}') can pass even when real work-sized prompts fail (context overflow, complex schema) — this only tests reachability/basic JSON compliance, not real-task competence
metrics.guard: never treated as a proxy for inference.output_failure_rate on real work; it only confirms an instrument is minimally reachable and JSON-compliant
metrics.verifier_note: Accurate as stated.

metrics.name: JSON-mode-rejected-then-retried rate
metrics.source: runesmith/instruments.py:342-345,362-363 (fallback logic and receipt field) — NOT in the ledger whitelist at runesmith/app/workspace.py:564-566, so it is invisible to any historical query today
metrics.min_sample: n/a until instrumented; 20+ calls per instrument once added
metrics.gaming_risk: none once recorded; the risk today is the opposite — this silently-recovered failure mode currently leaves no trace at all, so a provider that always needs the fallback looks identical to one that never does
metrics.guard: instrumentation needed: add 'json_mode_fallback' to the whitelisted fields in workspace.py:564-566 (or a dedicated ledger event)
metrics.verifier_note: This entry's own self-assessment is accurate -- it correctly identified the same class of whitelist gap several other 'recorded' claims in this catalogue missed.

metrics.name: Median call latency
metrics.definition: Minor fix: every logged instrument.call already represents one *completed* attempt -- there is no in-progress state logged, so a role invocation that eventually raises TransportCensored simply contributes several transport-labelled rows rather than being excluded. Also add 'instrument kind' as a mandatory slice: the 'manual' kind is a human relay (config.py's example gives it timeout_s=3600) and its latency is not comparable to an automated call -- pooling it would badly skew p50/p90.
metrics.source: runesmith/instruments.py:213-219 (latency measured started..response), 232 (_response(...,latency)); runesmith/app/workspace.py:564-566 ('latency_s' recorded per call)
metrics.min_sample: 30+ terminal calls per cell for a stable percentile estimate
metrics.gaming_risk: timing out early (shorter timeout_s) lowers measured latency for the calls that complete while pushing more into inference.transport_failure_rate — must be read together
metrics.guard: paired with inference.transport_failure_rate and inference.censor_rate
metrics.verifier_note: Formula and citation accurate; population wording was slightly imprecise and manual-relay latency wasn't called out as needing its own slice.

metrics.name: Tail call latency
metrics.definition: Same correction as inference.latency_p50_s (population wording, and add instrument-kind/'manual' slice).
metrics.source: same as inference.latency_p50_s
metrics.min_sample: 50+ terminal calls per cell — p90 needs more samples than p50 to be stable
metrics.gaming_risk: same as p50; additionally a router could hide a slow instrument by rarely selecting it, which lowers its own p90 sample size below the reporting minimum without fixing the slowness
metrics.guard: require the min_sample floor before reporting a p90 change as real; below it, report 'insufficient data' rather than a number
metrics.verifier_note: Same as latency_p50_s.

metrics.name: Share of calls served locally vs hosted
metrics.definition: Add two caveats: (1) the 'local' computation is only produced for a live config-listing call, not stored per instrument.call event, so joining a historical call's 'instrument' name to TODAY's config misclassifies any call made before that instrument's base_url/preset last changed (the same historical-join caveat this catalogue already applies to generation_over_generation_efficiency_trend, but not here). (2) 'local' (runs on this computer) is a different axis from 'free vs paid' -- Groq/OpenRouter/Gemini free tiers are hosted-but-free and would incorrectly read as 'not local' here even though they cost nothing; do not conflate the two.
metrics.source: runesmith/app/workspace.py:377-378 ('local': ... 'local' in preset or 127.0.0.1/localhost in base_url); joined against instrument.call's 'instrument' field
metrics.gaming_risk: none; purely describes the owner's current mix of free-local vs hosted work, useful context for reading model_class-sliced metrics, not a target itself
metrics.guard: n/a (diagnostic only)
metrics.verifier_note: Citation exact; definition needs the same historical-join caveat applied elsewhere in this catalogue, plus a warning against conflating 'local' with 'free'.

metrics.name: Milliner ticket queue dwell time
metrics.source: runesmith/milliner_jobs.py:106-108 (record['created']=now()), 84-87 (record.update(...,updated=now()) on terminal); fields exist in each <home>/inference-requests/*.json file but are not currently surfaced by accounting_view (runesmith/app/inference_accounting.py:109-125) or availability_view (runesmith/app/inference_availability.py)
metrics.gaming_risk: none directly; risk is in over-reading short windows before enough tickets resolve, since resolution can span minutes under load per FINDINGS.md's pacing note
metrics.guard: only compute over gateway_state='terminal' or 'refused' receipts (never 'pending'/'submitting'/'remote_outcome_unknown')
metrics.verifier_note: Accurate as stated.

metrics.name: Cost-tier declaration coverage
metrics.definition: count(configured instruments with a non-null, owner-set cost_tier field) / count(configured instruments). Diagnostic precondition for inference.unaudited_paid_spend_share, the free/paid half of inference.local_vs_hosted_split, and inference.weak_vs_strong_output_gap's model_class grouping -- none of which have a real machine-readable source for free_local/free_hosted/paid today.
metrics.source: runesmith/config.py:26-49 (DEFAULT_CONFIG instrument spec has no cost_tier key); runesmith/app/providers.py:18-71 (PRESETS has no such key either -- only the 'local' boolean and free-text blurbs).
metrics.min_sample: n/a -- a configuration-level count, not a sampled rate; report the raw count of instruments missing the field.
metrics.gaming_risk: none directly; the risk is only in not having this, which silently blocks every free/paid-tier-based measurement in this catalogue.
metrics.guard: n/a (diagnostic precondition, not itself optimised).

metrics.name: Ollama silent-truncation proxy rate
metrics.definition: Same intent, but persist the 'estimate' value (or a precomputed boolean) onto the receipt at instruments.py:429-433 and add it to the whitelist. A workaround using recorded 'tokens_in' against 'prompt_bytes'/3 is NOT equivalent -- prompt_bytes only covers the user prompt, not the system+schema text the real estimate includes, so it systematically understates the true estimate and would under-flag real truncation.

primary_sets.build: Optimise together, as one bundle, so none can be gamed alone: (1) build.first_attempt_success_rate and (2) build.calls_to_green (or build.time_to_green) as the primaries a build-pipeline trial (author_packet, planner_prompt phrasing that feeds draft_files, retry_policy, router_policy) tries to move — one for quality-on-first-try, one for cost/speed to a finished milestone. They are bundled with mandatory guardrails that must not regress when either primary improves: build.acceptance_pass_rate (blocks gaming success by only ever running the cheaper project_checks phase or by the owner's acceptance file quietly going missing), build.check_stale_rate and build.check_timeout_rate (blocks gaming speed by truncating check phases or racing a stale snapshot to a fast false 'passed'), build.draft_waste_rate and build.candidate_bytes_wasted (blocks gaming attempts_to_green by spawning many cheap throwaway drafts outside the counted ordinary-attempt ledger), and build.escalation_trigger_rate (blocks gaming the ordinary-path numbers by routing failures into the separately-counted one-shot escalation instead of fixing the ordinary path). build.apply_rate is a secondary primary only once the above four guardrails are flat: it is the only point where a passing check turns into shipped code, but it is easy to inflate by weakening acceptance criteria, so it must never be read without build.acceptance_pass_rate beside it. All other listed points are diagnostic or guardrail-only; none of them should be a trial's sole optimisation target.
primary_sets.inference: A self-improvement trial in this domain (repair_organ, router_policy, or the acceptance/check_proposer chain) should optimise the following together, never one alone: (1) inference.output_failure_rate — can this weak/cheap model actually produce a usable answer; (2) inference.cost_per_successful_call — what a usable answer costs in $ (or free-quota headroom) once accounting is reconciled; (3) inference.latency_p90_s — the slow tail, which is what an owner actually feels while waiting on a build. These three are cheap to game in isolation (reject hard calls to raise success%, starve retries to cut cost, time out early to cut latency), so every trial of them must be reported alongside these guardrails, which must not get worse: inference.transport_censor_rate and inference.pre_admission_refusal_rate (a role silently giving up more often is not an improvement), inference.binding_mismatch_rate (must stay at zero — this is a safety property of the ticket protocol, not a tunable), inference.token_accounting_completeness_rate and inference.aggregate_mismatch_rate (cost must stay honestly measured, not just measured lower), and — cross-domain — the build.checked pass rate for drafts authored under the changed route/organ (a cheaper, faster, 'successful' JSON answer that still fails the acceptance checker downstream is not a win; that pass-rate lives in the building/repair domain's ledger, not this one, and must be pulled in as the trial's real scoreboard).
primary_sets.mapping_planning: A self-improvement trial in this domain should optimise, together, at most: (1) mapping_planning.envmap.build_wall_seconds + files_per_second, guarded by mapping_planning.envmap.classification_accuracy and truncated_scan_rate (a faster mapper that starts misclassifying objects or silently truncating scans is not an improvement); (2) mapping_planning.breakdown.child_completion_rate, guarded by breakdown.adoption_rate and breakdown.rejection_rate (smaller steps that owners refuse to adopt, or that get adopted but still fail, are not progress); (3) mapping_planning.planner.milestone_completion_rate and plan_survival_rate, guarded by milestone_drop_rate, held_plan_rate and milestone_done_when_rate (a plan that finishes milestones by quietly dropping or vaguely defining them has not improved); (4) mapping_planning.selfmap.repair_yield (already the paper's C7 primary, owned by the repair-organ domain but read here through selfmap.py), guarded by false_promotion_rate, organ_error_rate and organ_timeout_rate. Every other metric below is diagnostic or a guardrail for one of these four, or is honestly marked needs_instrumentation because the receipt it would need does not exist yet.
primary_sets.checks: A self-improvement trial in this domain should optimize, together, the small cluster: checks.soundness_rate (the true target: fails before, passes two correct builds, fails every broken build) once the still-unbuilt reference-build check (checks.reference_build_pass_rate, design step 5) and mutation gate (checks.mutation_kill_rate, design step 6) exist to compute it on more than 3 hardcoded milestones; until then, its two cheap, already-recorded live proxies checks.dry_run_healthy_rate and checks.revision_yield/checks.retry_recovery_rate (does the pipeline's own one-shot safety net actually fix what it flags); plus checks.approval_rate and checks.milestone_coverage_rate (owner judgment: checks get made, and the owner actually trusts them); and, since the owner explicitly asked about cheap-model efficiency, checks.model_tier_soundness_gap (what a free/weak model achieves relative to a strong baseline on the same milestone). Every one of these must be held against guardrails that must not get worse when a primary improves: checks.over_specification_rate and checks.vacuity_rate (the two ways soundness can be faked -- too strict or too loose), checks.unstated_text_rate (hidden requirements), checks.calls_per_proposal and checks.time_to_approval (cost/latency), checks.discard_rate and checks.replace_rate (owner had to intervene), checks.both_answers_unusable_rate (catastrophic silent failure), and checks.localized_failure_rate (the FOOTER/PUBLIC_CRITERIA plumbing that makes any of this diagnosable at all must keep working). checks.scorer_coverage is the honesty guard on the whole set: no soundness claim generalizes past the milestones it actually covers.
primary_sets.self_improvement: A trial (a Kaizen-authored organ candidate on its way to activation) should be judged, together, on self_improvement.repair_yield (or self_improvement.seconds_per_success when the selected target is cycle_time, diagnose.py:116-123) and self_improvement.cost_per_activated_generation_opportunities — i.e. did delivered repairs (or delivered speed at held yield) actually go up, and how much of the owner's own opportunity stream and the model budget did it cost to find out. Both are guarded, simultaneously and non-negotiably, by self_improvement.false_promotion_rate (must not rise), the organ-error rate inside dev_score (kaizen/improve.py:321, must stay 0 — better() at improve.py:339 already refuses any organ_errors>0), self_improvement.kaizen_gain_to_noise_margin (the freeze must clear the incumbent's own replay-to-replay noise, loop.py:139-151), and self_improvement.post_activation_regression_rate (attention reverting to SUBJECT_BLOCKED soon after an activation, attention.py:128-133). self_improvement.trial_win_rate, self_improvement.kaizen_freeze_rate, self_improvement.affordance_coverage and self_improvement.mechanism_diversity_per_campaign are process/diagnostic signals only and must never be optimized directly: a Kaizen author (or a future community contributor chasing the scoreboard) can learn to pass its own gates — propose trivially "different" mechanisms to satisfy the diversity rule, or author changes shaped to beat freeze_rule's noise bar by luck rather than by repairing more — without any gain in what the owner's opportunities actually need, which is exactly the Goodhart risk COMMUNITY_EVOLUTION.md's scoreboard rule (points only for promoted AND replicated gains, docs/design/COMMUNITY_EVOLUTION.md:39-41) is designed to resist.
primary_sets.owner_reliability: A self-improvement trial in this domain should optimise, together: (1) owner_reliability.rescue_rate / zero_rescue_release_rate — can the target persona finish the journey's plan-build-check-apply-restart-continue loop alone; (2) owner_reliability.time_to_first_applied_change and owner_actions_to_first_value — how fast and with how few owner actions that happens; (3) owner_reliability.journey_pass_rate — whether the full protocol (JOURNEY_COVERAGE_PLAN.md section 6) passes end to end. These must never improve by weakening safety: pair them with the guardrails owner_reliability.invariant_violation_rate (I1-I10, especially I1 observe-leak and I4 unauthorized-write), layer1_sweep_pass_rate, path_escape_refusal_rate, key_exposure_rate, ledger_chain_integrity_rate, write_rollback_integrity_rate, support_report_consent_rate and support_report_scope_integrity (all must stay at their ceiling, ideally 1.0/0 as designed), plus friction_count_per_journey and bug_count_per_journey as a check against gaming rescue_rate by reclassifying real rescues as mere friction. A trial that raises the primaries while any guardrail regresses should be rejected regardless of the primary's gain.
primary_sets.project_scorecard:
Project-wide scorecard (the few numbers any single self-improvement trial, of any lever, must be judged against together -- not one alone):

1. e2e.milestone_lead_time_total (seconds, idea/milestone to applied) -- the owner's felt speed.
2. e2e.milestone_cost_usd (USD, same span) -- the owner's felt cost; report per-milestone median and p90, not just mean.
3. e2e.full_pipeline_success_rate (ratio) -- how often the whole journey goes clean, no corrections/escalations/revisions/discards.
4. e2e.throughput_per_hour (milestones/hour) -- the 'production iteration speed' the owner named directly.

Guardrails that must not get worse when any of the four primaries improves: checks.vacuity_rate and checks.over_specification_rate (a faster/cheaper pipeline must not come from a weaker or wronger acceptance gate); build.needs_revision_rate and e2e.rework_after_apply_rate (speed must not just move failure downstream to after 'applied'); self_improvement.false_promotion_rate (a generation that wins trials faster must not do so by winning wrongly); owner_reliability.rescue_rate and owner_reliability.invariant_violation_rate (nothing here may cost owner trust or safety); community.aggregate_only_leak_rate (once the community feature exists, no efficiency gain may leak project content).

How to judge ANY single-lever trial (repair_organ today; planner_prompt, check_proposer, router_policy, etc. once meta.lever_coverage rises above its current 1/12): (1) The trial's own local decision (self_improvement.trial_win_rate / trial_effect_size / trial_decision_p_value) is necessary but never sufficient -- it answers 'did the lever get better at its own narrow job', not 'did the owner's experience get better.' (2) Require meta.e2e_delta_per_generation to confirm a favorable move in at least the primary the lever plausibly affects, on matched milestones, independent of the trial's own arms. (3) Require the guardrail list above to hold or improve in the same window, checked via meta.guardrail_regression_incidence. (4) Track meta.local_proxy_transfer_rate over the project's history: if trial wins and e2e confirmations keep disagreeing, the trial's own success measure needs revisiting, since a persistently low transfer rate means the self-improvement loop is optimizing the wrong thing precisely, not imprecisely. (5) Weigh the win against meta.trial_roi (e2e gain per dollar/call spent running the campaign and trial itself) so self-improvement is never assumed free; self_improvement.evaluation_replay_cost and inference cost during the trial's own opportunities are real spend against the owner's configured self-improvement share (self_improvement.owner_share_utilization, sourced today from the fixed attention-mode SHARE_BP table in runesmith/kaizen/attention.py:46 -- there is no owner-facing 10%-90% dial in code yet, only the design intent in docs/design/COMMUNITY_EVOLUTION.md:42-44).

Why these four and not more: build/inference/mapping_planning/checks/self_improvement each already have precise stage-local primaries (build.first_attempt_success_rate, inference.cost_per_successful_call, mapping_planning.selfmap.repair_yield, checks.soundness_rate, self_improvement.repair_yield). Those stay as diagnostics that explain WHY an e2e primary moved. The four e2e primaries exist because none of the six domains, alone or summed, currently answer the owner's actual question -- from an idea to a change applied on the owner's machine, is Runesmith getting faster, cheaper, and more reliably right, and is a cheaper model closing that gap -- since every existing metric starts counting after planning/acceptance overhead is already spent, or stops counting before the owner's own review and rework are included.

build.verifier:
Reviewed all 65 build-pipeline metrics against the 14 assigned files plus JOURNEY_LOG.md. All cited ledger event names exist exactly as the master list states, and I independently confirmed every 'build.*' ledger.append call site across the file set. Findings, in order of importance:

1. One exact duplicate: build.needs_revision_rate == build.check_fail_rate (building.py:711 makes 'needs_revision' state and status='failed' the same condition; the catalogue's own guard text for needs_revision_rate literally says 'Same as build.check_fail_rate'). Recommend dropping needs_revision_rate.

2. A real double-counting bug in the primary metric build.calls_to_green (and its by_model slice): author-only revisions (author_revisions.py) write into the SAME 'build-attempts' folder as ordinary attempts (unlike escalation/correction/supplement, which have separate folders), so they get counted once as an 'ordinary author dispatch' and again as a 'revision dispatch'.

3. build.check_stale_rate was marked needs_instrumentation but is actually already recorded (every verify_draft return, stale or not, flows through _save_checked_draft's unconditional 'build.checked' ledger append at building.py:717-719, or review_current_files' 'build.current_files_checked' append) — the catalogue had it backwards on top of that, claiming _unchanged_verdict's cache-hit path should be included in the denominator when that function specifically exists (per JOURNEY_LOG.md's F14 note) to avoid calling verify_draft at all. What genuinely does need instrumentation is distinguishing the four separate stale causes and separately the interrupted-vs-timeout split within 'inconclusive' — added as build.stale_cause_distribution and build.check_interrupted_share.

4. build.replan_trigger_rate was marked 'recorded' but worker.py:538's outcome whitelist actually strips 'replan_needed' before writing job history to disk — the same gap the catalogue already (correctly) caught for build.allowance_exhaustion_rate, just missed here, with the two metrics' supporting line citations for the breakdown/advanced auto-enqueue blocks also swapped.

5. build.queue_wait_time and build.schedule_adherence_rate both cite a job['started'] field that is never persisted to STUDIO_JOBS.json history (it only exists transiently in STUDIO_CURRENT.json, removed on completion); both are still computable, but only via finished_iso − seconds, not the field named.

6. Several 'trigger_rate' metrics (escalation_trigger_rate, correction_trigger_rate, revision_trigger_rate) cite a stateless eligibility-query function (build_escalation_status, correction_candidates, revision_status) as if its 'eligible=True' result were itself a countable receipt; it isn't. correction_trigger_rate additionally had a factually wrong denominator (an OR-clause conflating admission-time refusal with unrelated post-hoc check failure).

7. snapshot_size_distribution and excluded_input_share both claimed availability that only holds for the narrow subset of checks that happen to freeze their snapshot (review_current_files, build_corrections) — the ordinary build_step/_check_and_record path never persists total bytes or the excluded-file list, only a file count.

8. build.apply_rate and build.apply_block_rate each have a real edge case worth naming precisely: _unchanged_verdict can produce a build.advanced with no accompanying fresh build.checked in the same window (a cache-hit reapply), and apply_block_rate's denominator currently mixes 'candidate went stale mid-check' with 'apply was never authorized in the first place' (added build.grant_mismatch_apply_skip_rate to separate the latter).

Beyond these, most of the 65 entries are substantively sound with only line-citation drift (typically 3-15 lines off the actual definition/ledger-append site, likely from a slightly different revision of building.py) — I corrected the specific line ranges wherever I verified them directly rather than flag every minor drift as an error. No metric was found to be unmeasurable even in principle. Added three new, precisely specified diagnostics/guardrails (build.check_interrupted_share, build.grant_mismatch_apply_skip_rate, build.stale_cause_distribution) that fill gaps surfaced during verification, each with an exact code citation for what still needs instrumenting.

notes.critic:
Scope and method: I am the completeness critic for cross-domain and end-to-end measurement, working from the six domains' full metric catalogue (build, inference, mapping_planning, checks, self_improvement, owner_reliability) supplied in the task. I opened only the files needed to confirm the joins an end-to-end metric would require, all under D:\Runesmith\: runesmith/ledger.py (event/hash-chain shape), runesmith/app/workspace.py (milestone.added/updated, goal.added/updated/removed, draft.created/applied, instrument.call), runesmith/app/building.py (build.* event sites and the draft-to-milestone linkage), runesmith/app/acceptance_proposals.py (acceptance.proposed/approved), runesmith/app/planner.py (the request_key = f'draft-{milestone_id}-{time.time_ns()}' construction, the load-bearing discovery of this review: milestone-level cost/call attribution is derivable from receipts already written, not a new instrumentation need), runesmith/kaizen/trial.py and runesmith/share.py (trial mechanics and cross-home generation import, confirming only the repair organ has a live trial path today), runesmith/kaizen/attention.py (SHARE_BP, confirming the owner's 10%-90% self-improvement dial described in the community doc is design intent, not yet built), runesmith/inference_usage.py (cost/token reconciliation states used to define e2e.milestone_cost_usd precisely), and docs/design/COMMUNITY_EVOLUTION.md in full (explicitly labelled 'idea and design direction, not built' at line 3, which is why every community.* metric here is needs_instrumentation).

The single most important structural finding: an end-to-end 'idea to applied' measure is mostly derivable today, not a green-field instrumentation project, because (a) the milestone id is embedded directly in the author request_key used as instrument.call's join key, and (b) the ledger's hash-chain already guarantees the receipts needed to reconstruct a milestone's full timeline cannot be silently edited. The two real gaps found: (1) no milestone-to-goal link exists yet (blocks e2e.idea_to_applied_yield and any 'idea' framing above the milestone level); (2) self-improvement (Kaizen/trial) exists only for the repair organ -- 11 of the 12 named levers (planner_prompt, milestone_breakdown, check_proposer, examples_template, router_policy, mapper, author_packet, context_focus, retry_policy, ui_wording, scheduler) have no trial-gated improvement path at all today, which meta.lever_coverage makes explicit and countable.

I did not re-derive or duplicate any metric already present in the six-domain catalogue (build.time_to_green, self_improvement.owner_share_utilization, self_improvement.cross_project_replication_count, checks.revision_yield were all left alone); every metric proposed here either spans more than one domain's event set, measures the self-improvement loop's effect on outcomes outside itself, or covers a community-pipeline stage not implied by any single domain's file set. Proposed 28 new metrics (11 e2e., 6 meta., 11 community.) plus 7 dimensions, deliberately fewer and load-bearing rather than padded, since the six domains already carry the volume and this pass exists to close the seams between them.
